source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Electrical, p.6Y-30

procedures.title: Starting circuit: resistance check
steps: Ground the distributor primary lead so the engine will not fire.

With the starter switch closed and the motor cranking, read voltage drop across each section: battery positive post to solenoid battery terminal; battery negative post to starter housing; solenoid battery terminal to solenoid motor terminal.
A drop over 0.2 volts in any section means excess resistance there; find and fix it.
Never crank continuously for more than 30 seconds, to avoid overheating.
If the solenoid will not pull in, close the starter switch and read the drop from the solenoid BATTERY terminal to its SWITCH terminal; over 3.5 volts means excess resistance in the control circuit.

If that drop is 3.5 volts or less and the solenoid still will not pull in, read the voltage at the SWITCH terminal; a cool solenoid should pull in at 7.7 volts or more (a warm one needs somewhat more).

specs.what: max voltage drop per starting circuit section

procedures.title: Starting motor and solenoid: check
steps: Only make these checks if battery specific gravity is 1.215 or higher.
If the solenoid does not pull in, read the voltage from the solenoid SWITCH terminal to ground with the starter switch closed; let a warm solenoid cool first.
Under 7.7 volts: look for excess resistance in the solenoid control circuit.

specs.what: minimum battery specific gravity for test
